content.title: World Baseball Classic Championship Trophy
content.text: From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia This article is about World Baseball Classic Trophy. For the current world championship organized from 2013, see World Baseball Classic. For the current Major League Baseball's championship trophy, see Commissioner's Trophy (MLB). World Baseball Classic Championship TrophySportBaseballAwarded forWinning the World Baseball ClassicPresented byWorld Baseball Classic Inc.World Baseball Softball ConfederationHistoryFirst winner Japan (2006)Most wins Japan (3 titles)Most recent Venezuela (2026)WebsiteWBCI.com The World Baseball Classic Championship Trophy[1][2] is the trophy presented by Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) (through World Baseball Classic Inc.) to the winning team of the World Baseball Classic. The trophy was created by Tiffany & Co.[3][4] From 2006 to 2023, there were a total of five trophies and three countries shared them. The WBC Championship Trophy The World Baseball Classic Trophy was produced by Tiffany & Co. craftsmen over 200 hours. It is originally made of sterling silver (with gold details added over time) by Tiffany & Co., a long-established silvery shop. Height: 25 inches (approximately 63.5 cm), Weight: 30 lbs (approximately 13.6 kg) Material: Silver (sterling silver) and 24-karat gold. The design motif is Global Baseball with the World Baseball Classic logo and consists of a pedestal, four boards, and balls. The pedestal cut into four tiers represents the tournament in the fourth round (first round, second round, semi-finals, and final), and the four sloping boards extending upward from the pedestal and the feather-shaped boards facing the upper center represent the four pools (first round). Also, the central baseball, supported by four boards, symbolizes the earth (global). Team Trophies Seasons Japan 3 2006, 2009, 2023 Venezuela 1 2026 United States 1 2017 Dominican Republic 1 2013 The 2006, 2009, and 2023 trophies are now in Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame,[5] Bunkyo Ward of Tokyo The 2017 trophy in National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum, Cooperstown, New York.
